title: Olaparib and bevacizumab maintenance
context_label: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)-positive advanced ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary-peritoneal cancer after first-line chemotherapy with bevacizumab
indication_text: First-line maintenance for HRD-positive FIGO III–IV high-grade epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary-peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response after platinum chemotherapy with bevacizumab.
purpose: Help sustain cancer control after first-line chemotherapy, using olaparib to target impaired DNA repair and bevacizumab to limit signals for new blood-vessel growth.
schedule_label: Daily olaparib tablets and bevacizumab every three weeks
schedule_summary: Take the prescribed olaparib dose morning and evening every day, including between infusion visits. Bevacizumab is given into a vein on Day 1 of each 21-day interval after the checks. The two medicines have separate stop dates.
administration_text: Olaparib usually starts at 300 mg by mouth twice daily, with reviewed dose changes if needed. Bevacizumab is 15 mg/kg by intravenous infusion every 21 days. Follow the individual prescription and the separate duration decisions.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every three weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated. Check urine protein and blood pressure before each bevacizumab cycle; monitor blood pressure after treatment as advised. Review symptoms, wounds, medicines and tablet supply; extra tests may be needed.

safety_note: Follow your own prescription and hospital contact plan. Dose changes and treatment restarts are decisions for your treating team.
urgent_extra: Call your oncology team urgently for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked weakness, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, a new painful swollen limb, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow your own temperature and contact plan; do not wait for the next appointment. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, seizures or stroke symptoms: call 112/999. Severe new abdominal pain, major bleeding, worsening wounds or severe headache/visual change also need urgent assessment; tell the infusion nurse immediately about symptoms during a visit.
anatomy_note: Selected medicine-specific effects, not a prediction of what will happen to you. Symptoms can occur on any day, including during a prescribed pause.
phases_note: The 21-day calendar shows one infusion interval and continuous tablets; it is not the total course length.
timeline_note: Treatment and review dates are shown; there are no predicted safe days or fixed side-effect windows.
treatment_scope_notice: NCCP 00746a–c · first-line maintenance with olaparib tablets and bevacizumab infusion
teachback: Which medicine is taken morning and evening, and which is given at an infusion visit?
When are blood, urine and blood-pressure checks due, and what are the two separate treatment endpoints?
Which symptoms, wounds or planned procedures mean contacting the team before the next visit?
consent_support: Discuss the expected maintenance benefit, uncertainty and alternatives. Olaparib risks include blood-count/marrow problems, lung inflammation, liver injury and clots. Bevacizumab adds high blood pressure, urine protein/kidney injury, bleeding/clots, wound-healing problems, perforation/fistula, infusion reactions, PRES, heart and fertility effects. Follow the olaparib pregnancy-prevention advice, including two reliable complementary methods where relevant. Bevacizumab also requires effective contraception during treatment and for six months after its last dose; use the later applicable end date. Do not breastfeed during either treatment, for at least six months after the last bevacizumab dose, and for one month after the last olaparib dose—whichever date is later. Discuss fertility before treatment and tell the team immediately if pregnancy is possible.

agents.name: Olaparib
agents.mechanism: Olaparib blocks poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP)-associated DNA repair and can trap PARP on DNA. Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) means an important DNA-repair pathway is already impaired, through a BRCA change or another qualifying pattern of genomic instability. Further disruption can make cancer cells less able to survive. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, so blood counts remain important.

risks: Anaemia, sometimes requiring transfusion; low white cells or platelets with infection or bleeding risk
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, diarrhoea, reduced appetite and changes in taste
Fatigue or weakness, headache, dizziness and mouth soreness
Serious persistent blood-count changes, including MDS/AML; the risk varies with the treatment setting and previous therapy
Pneumonitis: inflammation of the lungs that can be serious or fatal
Blood clots in veins or lungs; symptoms need urgent assessment
Liver injury and changes in kidney blood tests; the team may need to review treatment
Allergic reactions and harm to an unborn baby; discuss fertility, contraception and breastfeeding where relevant
agents.watch: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy.
visual: DNA damage accumulates in susceptible cells

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.mechanism: Bevacizumab binds vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a signal that encourages new blood vessels to form. Blocking this signal can limit blood-vessel growth that supports cancer. VEGF also matters in normal tissues, so blood pressure, urine protein and wound healing need attention.
agents.explanation: Bevacizumab binds vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a signal that encourages new blood vessels to form. Blocking this signal can limit blood-vessel growth that supports cancer. VEGF also matters in normal tissues, so blood pressure, urine protein and wound healing need attention.
risks: High blood pressure, including severe hypertension
Protein in urine and kidney problems, including nephrotic syndrome
Bleeding and blood clots in arteries or veins
Delayed wound healing and serious wound infection
A hole in the bowel or an abnormal connection between organs (perforation/fistula)
PRES: a serious brain condition that can cause headache, visual changes, confusion or seizures
Heart problems, impaired fertility and harm to an unborn baby
agents.watch: Tell the team about headache, visual changes, bleeding, new swelling, severe abdominal pain, wound problems or planned surgery. Keep blood-pressure medicines and urine checks as prescribed. No routine bevacizumab premedication is needed for everyone; previous reactions change the individual plan.
visual: Blood pressure, urine and healing are checked

anatomy: Olaparib can cause fatigue or headache. Severe headache, confusion, seizures or new vision changes need urgent assessment for severe blood-pressure effects or PRES with bevacizumab.
Olaparib can affect taste, appetite or the mouth. Report persistent soreness or bleeding; tell the team before dental procedures because bevacizumab can affect healing.
New cough or breathlessness may need assessment for infection, olaparib-related lung inflammation, bleeding or a clot. Chest pain or severe breathing difficulty needs emergency help.
Olaparib needs liver and kidney blood tests. Bevacizumab can cause protein loss through the kidneys, so urine tests are separate. Report jaundice, dark urine or new swelling.
Use prescribed sickness support for olaparib. Severe new abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or a swollen abdomen needs urgent assessment; bevacizumab can cause perforation or fistula.

Low red cells, white cells or platelets can cause tiredness, infection or bleeding. Persistent unexplained abnormalities may need specialist marrow tests; do not wait for the next routine review if unwell.
Report unusual bleeding and wounds that are slow to heal. Tell the team before surgery. Bevacizumab can impair healing; olaparib-related low platelets can also increase bleeding risk.
A new painful swollen limb needs urgent assessment. Stroke symptoms, chest pain, collapse or sudden severe breathlessness need emergency help.

phases.label: Maintenance
cycles: Individual maintenance plan; separate medicine clocks
phases.detail: The medicines have separate treatment clocks. Bevacizumab is given for a maximum of 15 months in total, counting doses with the earlier chemotherapy. Olaparib has a two-year disease-status review: complete treatment at two years if no cancer is visible on scans; if disease remains, the consultant may consider further benefit from continuing. Either medicine may stop earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects. Finishing bevacizumab does not automatically finish olaparib.

monitoring_schedule.note: Appointments are individual. Safety blood tests check treatment effects; scans and relevant cancer markers assess the disease. A reference calendar does not book an appointment or set the total course.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check red cells, infection-fighting white cells and platelets; persistent unexplained changes may need specialist tests.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before treatment and every three weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated; earlier for symptoms or abnormal results.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver profile
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check organ function and whether the prescription needs review.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before treatment and every three weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated.

monitoring_test_details.label: HRD and BRCA result
monitoring_test_details.purpose: HRD describes impaired repair of DNA breaks. A qualifying BRCA change or validated genomic-instability result can establish HRD for this pathway; a BRCA-wild-type result does not automatically mean HRD-negative.
monitoring_test_details.timing: A validated qualifying result is needed before treatment. Discuss any inherited implications with the team.

monitoring_test_details.label: Symptoms, scans and selected CA-125 tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess cancer control in the whole clinical picture, separate from safety blood tests.
monitoring_test_details.timing: The consultant sets symptom reviews, scans and any relevant CA-125 testing. Agree the total bevacizumab exposure and the separate two-year olaparib decision; safety blood/urine tests do not replace cancer assessment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Pregnancy testing where relevant
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Avoid exposing an unborn baby to olaparib.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting if you could become pregnant; repeat testing as advised.

monitoring_test_details.label: Blood pressure
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect and manage a bevacizumab effect on blood vessels; symptoms matter as well as readings.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Baseline, before each cycle and after treatment as advised; home checks if requested.

monitoring_test_details.label: Urine protein
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check whether bevacizumab is affecting the kidney filters; abnormal dipsticks can require a24-hour urine collection.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Baseline and before bevacizumab cycles; repeat/quantitative tests according to the team.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart assessment and selected echo
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Review cardiovascular risk; a heart ultrasound may be appropriate after anthracycline treatment or chest-wall radiotherapy.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Baseline history/examination; echo when indicated, rather than a universal serial echo timetable.

monitoring_test_details.label: INR if taking warfarin
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check the effect of prescribed warfarin and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Weekly until the warfarin dose is stable, then before each cycle; other anticoagulants need their own review.

support.title: Your prescribed sickness plan
support.text: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy.

support.title: Check every new medicine
support.text: Give the pharmacist a complete list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines and St John’s wort can change how much olaparib reaches your body. Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.

support.title: Blood counts and extra support
support.text: Blood counts check red cells that carry oxygen, white cells that help fight infection and platelets that help stop bleeding. Low counts can lead to a pause, a lower prescribed dose, a transfusion or further tests. Persistent or unexplained changes sometimes need specialist bone-marrow tests to investigate myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukaemia (MDS/AML). These are serious conditions; their risk differs by treatment setting and previous therapy. A treatment pause is not itself a diagnosis. There is no automatic white-cell injection, antibiotic or steroid course for everyone.

support.title: Eating, drinking and daily life
support.text: Ask for help early if nausea, mouth soreness, taste changes or poor appetite affect eating. Keep the team informed about weight loss or difficulty drinking. Fatigue may need a dose or blood-count review. Do not drive or use machinery if dizzy, weak or very tired.

support.title: A treatment pause
support.text: A prescribed pause can give blood counts or symptoms time to improve. It does not mean treatment has failed. Keep the agreed tests and ask exactly when the team will review restarting. Never take catch-up tablets.

support.title: Support for your wider treatment
support.text: Tell the team before any planned operation, dental procedure or new wound. Bevacizumab affects healing; a passed surgery date does not mean a wound is healed. Continue prescribed blood-pressure treatment and bring any requested readings. Blood thinners and all new medicines need review because bleeding/clotting risks must be considered together.

support.title: Fertility, contraception and breastfeeding
support.text: Follow the olaparib pregnancy-prevention advice, including two reliable complementary methods where relevant. Bevacizumab also requires effective contraception during treatment and for six months after its last dose; use the later applicable end date. Do not breastfeed during either treatment, for at least six months after the last bevacizumab dose, and for one month after the last olaparib dose—whichever date is later. Discuss fertility before treatment and tell the team immediately if pregnancy is possible.

support.title: Blood-pressure and urine follow-up
support.text: Continue only the blood-pressure medicines prescribed for you. Ask what readings or symptoms need contact and whether home measurement is wanted. Urine protein may have no obvious symptoms, so keep the tests even when feeling well.

support.title: Infusion support
support.text: Bevacizumab has minimal emetic potential. Routine steroid or antihistamine premedication is not required for everyone; the team changes the plan if there has been a previous reaction. Report flushing, rash, chest tightness, breathing difficulty or faintness during the infusion immediately.

sections.title: Before the first dose
sections.text: Confirm the validated HRD result, response after first-line platinum-taxane chemotherapy with bevacizumab, and recovery. Check full blood count, kidney/liver profile, blood pressure, urine protein, medicines and pregnancy testing where relevant; review heart health, bleeding/clots, operations and wound healing.

sections.title: How maintenance fits after chemotherapy
sections.text: Maintenance follows the first platinum-taxane and bevacizumab phase. The regimen specifies 6–9 platinum-taxane cycles and bevacizumab in the final chemotherapy cycles, with an interval-surgery allowance. Your team confirms the exact previous-treatment and recovery requirements before this combination starts.

sections.title: A practical home routine
sections.text: Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with or without food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. The usual starting dose is two 150 mg tablets each time (300 mg twice daily); your own dose may be lower. Check both tablet strength and tablet count after every prescription change. If you miss a dose, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double up. Do not substitute olaparib capsules for tablets. Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist. Bevacizumab needs an intravenous cannula or suitable existing access. The team explains how long the visit and checks will take.

sections.title: The written support plan
sections.text: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy. Give the pharmacist a complete list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines and St John’s wort can change how much olaparib reaches your body. Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.

sections.title: If treatment is paused
sections.text: Ask why it is paused, which tests are next and when the team will contact you. Only the prescriber can confirm the restart dose. Do not take catch-up tablets.

sections.title: Reviewing benefit and the next step
sections.text: The medicines have separate treatment clocks. Bevacizumab is given for a maximum of 15 months in total, counting doses with the earlier chemotherapy. Olaparib has a two-year disease-status review: complete treatment at two years if no cancer is visible on scans; if disease remains, the consultant may consider further benefit from continuing. Either medicine may stop earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects. Finishing bevacizumab does not automatically finish olaparib. The consultant sets symptom reviews, scans and any relevant CA-125 testing. Agree the total bevacizumab exposure and the separate two-year olaparib decision; safety blood/urine tests do not replace cancer assessment.

sections.title: Genetic results and family questions
sections.text: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A germline change is present in the body’s cells and may have implications for relatives. A tumour-only change does not by itself show that it is inherited. Ask which test you had, what the result means and whether genetic counselling is appropriate. A variant of uncertain significance is not automatically a treatment-qualifying result.

sections.title: Before leaving the clinic
sections.text: Confirm the next tests, review, tablet supply and verified daytime/out-of-hours contact numbers. Ask what to do if a result or prescription has not arrived.

sections.title: Infusion time
sections.text: The first bevacizumab infusion is usually 90 minutes. If tolerated, the second may take 60 minutes and later infusions 30 minutes. Checks, preparation and observation add to the visit; your unit confirms the actual schedule.

sections.title: Operations and wounds
sections.text: Tell the team before any planned operation, dental procedure or new wound. Bevacizumab affects healing; a passed surgery date does not mean a wound is healed. Continue prescribed blood-pressure treatment and bring any requested readings. Blood thinners and all new medicines need review because bleeding/clotting risks must be considered together.

chapters.title: Why this treatment is used
chapters.intro: Help sustain cancer control after first-line chemotherapy, using olaparib to target impaired DNA repair and bevacizumab to limit signals for new blood-vessel growth.

items.title: The treatment setting
items.text: This pathway requires a validated homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)-positive result, defined by a qualifying BRCA1/2 change and/or genomic instability, and response after first-line platinum chemotherapy with bevacizumab. HRD can be positive without a BRCA mutation. The team also checks histology, previous cycles, fitness and no previous PARP-inhibitor treatment.

items.title: What your test result means
items.text: HRD describes impaired repair of DNA breaks. A qualifying BRCA change or validated genomic-instability result can establish HRD for this pathway; a BRCA-wild-type result does not automatically mean HRD-negative. BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A germline change is present in the body’s cells and may have implications for relatives. A tumour-only change does not by itself show that it is inherited. Ask which test you had, what the result means and whether genetic counselling is appropriate. A variant of uncertain significance is not automatically a treatment-qualifying result.

items.title: How olaparib works
items.text: Olaparib blocks poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP)-associated DNA repair and can trap PARP on DNA. Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) means an important DNA-repair pathway is already impaired, through a BRCA change or another qualifying pattern of genomic instability. Further disruption can make cancer cells less able to survive. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, so blood counts remain important.

items.title: How bevacizumab works
items.text: Bevacizumab binds vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a signal that encourages new blood vessels to form. Blocking this signal can limit blood-vessel growth that supports cancer. VEGF also matters in normal tissues, so blood pressure, urine protein and wound healing need attention.

items.text: Kidney function, side effects and interacting medicines can change the prescription. A lower dose or pause is an individual safety decision. Do not copy someone else’s dose or restart because a calendar date has passed.

items.title: Wider care
items.text: Tell the team before any planned operation, dental procedure or new wound. Bevacizumab affects healing; a passed surgery date does not mean a wound is healed. Continue prescribed blood-pressure treatment and bring any requested readings. Blood thinners and all new medicines need review because bleeding/clotting risks must be considered together.

items.title: Fertility and pregnancy prevention
items.text: Follow the olaparib pregnancy-prevention advice, including two reliable complementary methods where relevant. Bevacizumab also requires effective contraception during treatment and for six months after its last dose; use the later applicable end date. Do not breastfeed during either treatment, for at least six months after the last bevacizumab dose, and for one month after the last olaparib dose—whichever date is later. Discuss fertility before treatment and tell the team immediately if pregnancy is possible.

chapters.title: Symptoms that need action
chapters.intro: A new symptom can have several causes; contact the team so it can be assessed.

items.title: When to call
items.text: Call your oncology team urgently for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked weakness, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, a new painful swollen limb, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow your own temperature and contact plan; do not wait for the next appointment. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, seizures or stroke symptoms: call 112/999.

items.title: Lungs and blood clots
items.text: New or worsening cough, breathlessness, chest pain or a painful swollen limb can signal infection, lung inflammation or a clot. Do not assume these symptoms are routine fatigue.

items.title: Liver and blood changes
items.text: Yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, unexplained severe fatigue, infections, bruising or bleeding need prompt advice. Persistent symptoms still matter during a treatment break or after treatment ends.

items.title: Abdominal pain, wounds and bleeding
items.text: Severe new abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, a swollen abdomen, major bleeding or a wound that is deteriorating requires urgent contact. Tell the team about planned surgery or dental procedures before they happen.

items.title: Headache, vision and neurological symptoms
items.text: Severe headache, new visual disturbance, confusion, seizures or stroke symptoms need urgent assessment. These may relate to severe hypertension, a clot or PRES; do not try to diagnose the cause yourself.

chapters.title: Evidence and your choices
chapters.intro: Trial results describe groups and should support a discussion about your priorities.

items.title: PAOLA-1: adding olaparib to bevacizumab maintenance
items.text: In the HRD-positive subgroup, median time without progression or death was 37.2 months with olaparib plus bevacizumab versus 17.7 months with placebo plus bevacizumab. These subgroup results support the selected pathway; a median is a group midpoint, not a deadline or an individual forecast.

items.title: What the comparison cannot tell us
items.text: The trial did not include an olaparib-only maintenance arm, so this comparison does not prove that the combination is better than olaparib alone. HRD subgroup analyses were not included in the trial’s multiple-testing procedure. Results cannot be transferred to HRD-negative disease or a later relapse.

items.title: Your priorities
items.text: Ask about expected benefit, side effects, alternatives including symptom-focused care, and choosing to decline or stop treatment. Decisions can be revisited as your health or priorities change.

evidence.title: PAOLA-1: adding olaparib to bevacizumab maintenance
evidence.intro: PAOLA-1 studied 806 people after response to first-line platinum-taxane chemotherapy with bevacizumab. Everyone continued bevacizumab; the randomised addition was olaparib or placebo. The figures below describe the HRD-positive subgroup.
evidence.population: HRD-positive advanced ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary-peritoneal cancer after first-line response
evidence.comparison: Olaparib plus bevacizumab versus placebo plus bevacizumab; 2019 HRD-positive subgroup analysis

These subgroup results support the selected pathway; a median is a group midpoint, not a deadline or an individual forecast.

questions.q: What is the aim of maintenance treatment?
questions.a: Help sustain cancer control after first-line chemotherapy, using olaparib to target impaired DNA repair and bevacizumab to limit signals for new blood-vessel growth. Maintenance follows the first platinum-taxane and bevacizumab phase. The regimen specifies 6–9 platinum-taxane cycles and bevacizumab in the final chemotherapy cycles, with an interval-surgery allowance. Your team confirms the exact previous-treatment and recovery requirements before this combination starts.

questions.q: How long will I take olaparib?
questions.a: The medicines have separate treatment clocks. Bevacizumab is given for a maximum of 15 months in total, counting doses with the earlier chemotherapy. Olaparib has a two-year disease-status review: complete treatment at two years if no cancer is visible on scans; if disease remains, the consultant may consider further benefit from continuing. Either medicine may stop earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects. Finishing bevacizumab does not automatically finish olaparib.

questions.q: How do I take it and what if I miss a dose?
questions.a: Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with or without food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. The usual starting dose is two 150 mg tablets each time (300 mg twice daily); your own dose may be lower. Check both tablet strength and tablet count after every prescription change. If you miss a dose, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double up. Do not substitute olaparib capsules for tablets. Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist.

Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every three weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated. Check urine protein and blood pressure before each bevacizumab cycle; monitor blood pressure after treatment as advised. Review symptoms, wounds, medicines and tablet supply; extra tests may be needed. The consultant sets symptom reviews, scans and any relevant CA-125 testing. Agree the total bevacizumab exposure and the separate two-year olaparib decision; safety blood/urine tests do not replace cancer assessment.

Call your oncology team urgently for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked weakness, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, a new painful swollen limb, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow your own temperature and contact plan; do not wait for the next appointment. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, seizures or stroke symptoms: call 112/999. Severe new abdominal pain, major bleeding, worsening wounds or severe headache/visual change also need urgent assessment; tell the infusion nurse immediately about symptoms during a visit.

questions.q: Does a tumour result mean the change is inherited?
questions.a: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A germline change is present in the body’s cells and may have implications for relatives. A tumour-only change does not by itself show that it is inherited. Ask which test you had, what the result means and whether genetic counselling is appropriate. A variant of uncertain significance is not automatically a treatment-qualifying result.

questions.q: What should I know before taking support medicines?
questions.a: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy. Give the pharmacist a complete list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines and St John’s wort can change how much olaparib reaches your body. Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.

questions.q: Why are the medicines stopped at different times?
questions.a: The medicines have separate treatment clocks. Bevacizumab is given for a maximum of 15 months in total, counting doses with the earlier chemotherapy. Olaparib has a two-year disease-status review: complete treatment at two years if no cancer is visible on scans; if disease remains, the consultant may consider further benefit from continuing. Either medicine may stop earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects. Finishing bevacizumab does not automatically finish olaparib.

questions.q: What happens if I need an operation?
questions.a: Tell the team before any planned operation, dental procedure or new wound. Bevacizumab affects healing; a passed surgery date does not mean a wound is healed. Continue prescribed blood-pressure treatment and bring any requested readings. Blood thinners and all new medicines need review because bleeding/clotting risks must be considered together.

questions.q: Why do I need urine and blood-pressure tests?
questions.a: Bevacizumab affects blood-vessel signalling and can raise blood pressure or cause protein to leak through kidney filters. These problems may not cause obvious symptoms, so tests matter even when you feel well.

phases.title: Daily olaparib
phases.text: Prescribed tablets morning and evening, every day. Planned two-year disease-status decision; earlier review for progression or side effects.

phases.title: Bevacizumab visits
phases.text: Infusion every three weeks. Maximum 15 months in total, including the earlier chemotherapy phase; its endpoint is separate from olaparib.

monitoring.when: Confirm HRD, response, full blood count, kidney/liver tests, blood pressure, urine protein, medicines and wound/surgery history.
Blood count/kidney/liver tests every three weeks for 12 months; urine and blood pressure before each bevacizumab cycle. Extra checks if indicated.
Individual consultant plan; count all bevacizumab exposure and review olaparib at two years.

cycle_expectations: Symptoms may occur on any day; there is no planned rest week. Report new problems promptly.
Use only your prescribed sickness/rescue medicines. Call if vomiting, diarrhoea or poor intake persists; do not wait for the next review.
preparation: Bring the medicine list and report planned surgery, wounds, bleeding/clots or blood-pressure symptoms.
Confirm prescribed support, tablet supply, the next infusion/checks and verified contact numbers.
